module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Pointwise.Set.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Lattice
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Defs

@[expose] public section

open Pointwise

/--
A covering system of a semiring `R` is a finite set of cosets of non-zero ideals whose union
covers the whole ring. In the case where `R = ℤ`, this corresponds to a choice of finitely many
congruence relations such that every integer satisfies at least one of the relations.
-/
structure CoveringSystem (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] where
  ι : Type
  [fintypeIndex : Fintype ι]
  residue : ι → R
  moduli : ι → Ideal R
  unionCovers : ⋃ i, ({residue i} : Set R) + (moduli i : Set R) = @Set.univ R
  ne_bot : ∀ i, moduli i ≠ ⊥
  ne_top : ∀ i, moduli i ≠ ⊤

/--
We say a covering system is strict if all the congruence relations that define it are take modulo
a different ideal (or number).

Note: this corresponds to the notion of a covering system that Erdos was using in
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
-/
structure StrictCoveringSystem (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] extends CoveringSystem R where
  injective_moduli : moduli.Injective

namespace CoveringSystem

variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

def coset (c : CoveringSystem R) (i : c.ι) : Set R :=
  {c.residue i} + c.moduli i

@[simp]
theorem iUnion_cosets (c : CoveringSystem R) : ⋃ i, c.coset i = Set.univ :=
  c.unionCovers

end CoveringSystem

findings.description: The docstring at lines 27–29 says the cosets use nonzero ideals, but the structure additionally requires every ideal to be proper (`ne_top`, line 38). Literally, the prose permits the single coset `0 + ℤ` of the nonzero ideal `⊤`, whereas `CoveringSystem ℤ` correctly excludes it. This is a documentation omission, not a defect in the intended mathematical implementation.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), §3, p. 24, defines covering congruences with `1 < n₁ < ⋯ < nᵣ` (https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf). Over ℤ, excluding `⊤` excludes modulus 1. The scratch file verifies that `(⊤ : Ideal ℤ) ≠ ⊥` and `{0} + (⊤ : Ideal ℤ) = Set.univ`, so nonzeroness alone does not express the implemented restriction.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “cosets of non-zero ideals” to “cosets of nonzero proper ideals”. Retain the `ne_top` field; optionally make the corresponding restriction to integer moduli greater than 1 explicit.

reformulations.difference: At `R = ℤ`, the source uses an increasing sequence of integer moduli greater than 1; Lean instead uses a finite indexed family of nonzero proper ideals with an injective modulus map.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonzero proper ideal of ℤ is uniquely `mℤ` for a natural number `m > 1`. Equality of these ideals is equality of their positive generators, and membership in `a + mℤ` is precisely congruence to a modulo m. Thus injectivity gives distinct numeric moduli, and the finite family can be enumerated in increasing order. Conversely, a classical covering system supplies all the structure fields. The ideal-normalization, equality, bound, and coset characterizations were proved in scratch Lean; the final sorting/reindexing equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Odd moduli are expressed by `¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2}`, rather than by an explicit `Odd` predicate on numeric moduli.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing each ideal uniquely as `(m)` with `m > 1`, Mathlib gives `(m) ≤ (2) ↔ 2 ∣ m`. Its negation is exactly oddness. The additional `C.moduli i ≠ ⊤` repeats an existing structure field. `CoverReview.erdos7_ideal_form_iff` in the scratch file proves the equivalence of the existential covering-system conditions with explicit natural moduli greater than 1 and odd.

reformulations.difference: The solved variant uses `StrictCoveringSystem ℕ`, whereas the source discusses covering all integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The specified ideals are principal, generated by `p - 1 ≥ 2`. An integer cover gives a natural-number translate cover after reducing each representative to `[0,m)`. Conversely, a finite natural-number translate cover gives congruence classes covering ℕ, and periodicity modulo the product of the moduli extends that cover to all of ℤ. Distinctness and the prime-minus-one restrictions are preserved. The scratch file proves a general equivalence for principal strict covers with any predicate on their natural moduli, and then the exact ℕ-versus-ℤ equivalence for this variant as `CoverReview.erdos273_three_nat_iff_int`.

review.notes: Checked all four explicit library declarations, their fields, and all five theorem uses in the four dependent problem files. No mathematical misformalization was found. Mathlib has no competing covering-system definition in this checkout, and the coset operation agrees with its pointwise-set convention. Boundary checks cover empty indices, trivial semirings, fields, moduli 0 and 1, negative integers, and unreduced natural representatives; the latter do not invalidate the existential use in Erdős 273. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors and contains the equivalence proofs plus an explicit 12-class cover with permitted moduli dividing 360, verified by `decide` and extended to all naturals. The principal equivalence proofs and constructed cover depend only on Lean's standard axioms, not `sorryAx`. A separate check verifies that the sigma inequality in Erdős 277 excludes n = 0. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review; no repository files were edited.
